findings.issue: The /audit:worktree row still says 'a second tree for the same task is refused'. P124.15-k2x changed task-add to adopt a tree already marked for the task (manage-worktrees.py do_task_add -> adopt_task_tree), and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md was updated to say so. The README is shipped user-facing text and now contradicts the code.
findings.resolution: Reword the row: a task that already has a marked tree gets that tree back at its recorded base, with its setup run again unless the marker records it completed.

findings.issue: close_wave moves every tree still standing into state.keptTrees, including a done member's tree kept because it holds a discarded undeclared change. Only a later task-add for that same task pops the entry, and a done task is never re-added, so the entry stays in the driver state for the life of the phase and is named once, in the wave-closing print. Nothing later lists a kept tree for a human to clean up.
findings.resolution: Name keptTrees again in the sign-off hand-off or in /audit:doctor, or record the path on the task's journal row, so a discarded change's tree is findable after the print scrolls away.

R3 is closed: do_task_add finds a marked tree before the non-empty-path check and adopts it; the marker records setup as pending until the setup returns and then its status, so a crash or a failed setup is re-provisioned before dispatch with no attempt spent (wt1-wt4); close_wave carries a blocked member's tree into keptTrees and add_tree adopts it at the base its marker records (wt5, wt6). integrate-task reads the base from the marker, so an adopted tree cut at an older base integrates against that base, not the new wave's. R4 is closed: wt8 exercises discard-then-close and asserts the tree survives, holds the undeclared bytes and is named; wt8m is a red twin that replaces tree_holds_only_integrated and sees the tree removed.
